To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
retinal detachment causes proliferation of virtually every retinal cell type, and that this proliferation begins within 2 hr of detachment and peaks at 3-4 days.
retinal detachment induces cellular proliferation in the detached retina, in the attached retina, and in the RPE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular response of the retina to retinal detachment.
the cellular and molecular mechanisms that underlie retinal degeneration and the development of neovascularization and fibrosis in response to retinal detachment.
the cellular and molecular events associated with retinal degenerations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

retinal detachment induces cellular proliferation in the retina, and the proliferating cells are not only Müller cells but also other non-neuronal cells, such as astrocytes, microglial cells, endothelial cells, and pericytes.

the proliferative response to experimental detachment in the cat retina is a complex, dynamic process, which involves virtually every cell type in the retinal parenchyma and the RPE, and which is characterized by a peak response that occurs within 4 days of detachment and which then subsides over the following 2 weeks.
retinal detachment is a very potent stimulus for retinal cell proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
retinal detachments are associated with a rapid and widespread proliferation of nonneuronal cells in the retina and RPE.
retinal detachment is a very potent stimulus for cellular proliferation, and that this proliferative response is not restricted to any one cell type.
retinal detachment induces a complex cellular and molecular response in the retina and retinal pigment epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retina is not a passive tissue.
retinal detachment is an inflammatory response that involves the proliferation of all cell types except for the photoreceptors and ganglion cells.
the RPE and retina are very plastic and can respond to injury by proliferation.
